name: Bullous Lichen Planus

criteria.description: Presence of violaceous, polygonal, flat-topped papules and plaques with superimposed tense bullae
Interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration and subepidermal blister formation on skin biopsy
Direct immunofluorescence showing linear IgG and/or C3 deposits along the basement membrane zone

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation plus histopathological confirmation; immunofluorescence supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from lichen planus pemphigoides and bullous pemphigoid is essential

laboratory: Histopathology showing basal cell degeneration and subepidermal blister
Direct immunofluorescence with linear IgG and/or C3 at basement membrane
other: Negative serology for bullous pemphigoid autoantibodies in some cases
Response to corticosteroids and immunosuppressive therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Widespread tense bullae without typical lichen planus papules
Positive circulating anti-BP180 and BP230 antibodies
Bullae arising both on lichen planus lesions and normal skin
Immunofluorescence findings similar to bullous pemphigoid
Distinct clinical course with mixed features

redFlags: Rapidly spreading bullous lesions with systemic symptoms
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or fever
Mucosal involvement causing significant pain or dysphagia
references: Wang, J. et al. Bullous lichen planus: clinical and immunopathological features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Bolognia, J. et al. Dermatology. 4th Edition. Elsevier, 2018.
